fixes.correction: Over the Dutch camp, fly ONLY the plain red-white-blue horizontal tricolour seen in panels 2.1 and 2.2, with no lettering or emblem. Do not show a white flag anywhere, because it would read as surrender, and do not show a plain blue flag. Keep Nagoji exactly as drawn: same face (thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud), rust-red turban, cream tunic, broad red sash, cream trousers, boots, talwar, his boot up on the log and his hand on the wattle parapet. Give him a calm, level gaze fixed on the Dutch palisade and tents, not lifted to the sky. Nagoji must be the ONLY figure in a rust-red turban or red sash. Draw the soldiers beside him in the trench like the troops on the same parapet in 2.2, in white turbans and indigo quilted tunics, or as bare-headed Nair infantry with forward-tied topknots. None of them wears a red turban, red sash or red waistband. Keep the same sunlit trench, wattle revetment, cannon and shot, and leave the open sky upper right clear for two balloons.
fixes.issues: Nagoji himself is on-model: curled moustache, clean chin, gold stud and the full commander kit. The panel still fails on setting and continuity. (1) The Dutch camp flies a plain WHITE flag and a plain BLUE flag instead of the plain red-white-blue tricolour that the chapter locks require and that 2.1 and 2.2 show. A white flag over the enemy camp reads as surrender or parley, which contradicts this beat ('they are afraid to admit...') and steps on the real parley later in the chapter. (2) Two soldiers beside him in the trench wear rust-red turbans, and one also has a red waistband, so they read as Nagoji lookalikes. This also breaks continuity with 2.2, where the troops on the same parapet wear white turbans and indigo tunics. (3) Minor: his gaze drifts up into the sky rather than resting on the enemy camp.

fixes.correction: Reverse the direction of travel and make it stealthy. The low, narrow, soot-blackened boats are COMING IN from the open sea toward the beach, bows angled toward the camera, with the paddlers facing the viewer. No one is pushing a boat into the surf and no boat is being launched. Keep the wide, low camera at the waterline looking out from the beach, which is empty, with no Nagoji in this panel. Show four or five boats strung out across the black swells as dark silhouettes. Their paddles dip cleanly with almost no spray. The oiled bodies of the Mukkuvar men catch only a faint wet sheen. Keep the surf mostly black with thin lines of foam rather than big white breakers, so the image reads quiet and shadowy. Keep the monsoon cloud over a faint moon, the palm-lined headland at the left edge, the 1740s Malabar fishermen in white loincloths and the large dark, empty sky across the top third for the caption.
fixes.issues: v01 shows the wrong direction and the wrong mood. In the foreground, men push a boat out into heavy, splashing surf, and every boat in the background is paddling away from the beach. That contradicts 3.2, where the same men drag a craft up the sand on their return from the raid, and it contradicts the script beat: shadows on black surf, boats slipping in almost without a splash. Apart from that it works: night, cloud over the moon, dark low boats, oiled Mukkuvar men in loincloths, a wide frame and plenty of empty sky for the caption. No text, gore or anachronism.

fixes.correction: Redraw Antony to match the Antony of panel 3.3 exactly. He is lean, tall and wiry, older, with curly black hair swept back and NO headband, a short grizzled beard and moustache, a pale nick through one eyebrow, rope scars across both forearms and a small wooden cross on a thin cord at his neck. He is oiled and bare-chested, in a white loincloth only, with no scar on cheek or jaw. Make his action a lazy, unhurried shrug: one shoulder lifted, mouth closed or in a dry half-smile, eyes calm and heavy-lidded, one hand loosely flicked open toward the dark sea behind him. Do not make him alarmed or urgent. Keep everything else as it is: Nagoji on the left in the commander look (rust-red turban, cream tunic, broad red sash, cream trousers, boots, talwar, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin with no stubble, small gold ear stud) with his hand at his chin, the same night beach, boats and fishermen, and the wide empty cloudy sky across the top for three balloons.
fixes.issues: Nagoji is correct (commander look, curled moustache, clean chin, gold ear stud, hand to chin), and the beach, night lighting and sky space are all good. Antony, however, is drawn as a different man from the Antony in 3.3 on the same page. He wears a cloth headband, has a full black beard and a heavier build, and has no wooden cross, no eyebrow nick and no visible forearm rope scars. Readers will not recognise him as the headman who spoke one panel earlier. His wide-eyed, open-mouthed, urgent look also goes against the script's shrug and the page note asking for a dry, unhurried Antony.

fixes.correction: Fly only ONE flag over the Dutch camp, and make it the plain Dutch horizontal tricolour of three equal bands: RED on top, WHITE in the middle, BLUE at the bottom, with no emblem. Draw no blue-white-blue flag, no white or pale flag and no second flag anywhere on the beach. The defenders on our side of the parapet are Nair infantry: young, bare-chested, short white mundu, hair in a forward-tied topknot (kudumi) on the front of the head, with NO turbans, head cloths, vests or shirts. They hold spears or matchlocks. Keep everything else as drawn: the view over our palm-revetted parapet; the Dutch camp's sagging mud ramparts; the one cannon tilted into slumped earth; sick men lying under torn canvas; empty barrels stacked by the wall; and, small in frame among the sick, the short dark-haired Dutch officer in a blue coat with an officer's sash. Keep the sea behind and open, low-detail sky across the top third for the two captions. Use warm late-afternoon light, so the page moves from the dusk of the previous panel toward evening.
fixes.issues: The beat itself is well drawn: sagging mud ramparts, one cannon tilted into slumped earth, sick men under torn canvas, stacked barrels, a small dark-haired officer among the sick, and open sky for the captions. But the large flag over the Dutch camp is blue-white-blue (it reads as Argentina). It contradicts the chapter lock (Dutch flags are plain red-white-blue tricolours) and the correct tricolour over the same camp in 4.1 on this page. A second small blue flag stands on the beach. Our defenders in the foreground wear white turbans, vests and shirts, against the chapter's Nair infantry lock (forward-tied topknot, bare chest, short white mundu, no turban). The frame is also in hard midday light, between the dusk of 4.1 and the evening of 4.4.

fixes.correction: Draw no white, cream or pale flag anywhere, because it reads as surrender, the opposite of this beat. If a flag flies over the Dutch stockade, it is the plain Dutch horizontal tricolour (RED top, WHITE middle, BLUE bottom); otherwise draw no flag. Drop the close foreground of our soldiers: no turbaned or vested men and no muzzle flash or gun smoke from our side. At most, show a low strip of our palm-revetted parapet along the bottom edge. Show visible heat shimmer over the open sand between us and the Dutch wall. Make the thin, ragged volley come clearly from the Dutch palisade itself: a few small, scattered white musket puffs along the wall near the tall officer. Keep De Lannoy exactly as drawn: distant, tall, bareheaded so his pale hair catches the light, in a torn and soot-stained Dutch blue coat. He paces the perimeter, pointing and pushing shorter dark-haired blue-coated soldiers into a gap, too far away for a readable face. Keep the open sky in the upper third clear for the caption.
fixes.issues: De Lannoy himself is right: distant, tall, bareheaded with pale hair, in a torn and soot-stained blue coat, pointing as he drives shorter dark-haired soldiers along the palisade. But a large off-white, stained flag flies over the Dutch stockade. It reads as a white flag of surrender, the opposite of the caption 'Yet they held.', and it breaks the red-white-blue tricolour lock and 4.1. The frame is dominated by our turbaned, vest-wearing musketeers, which breaks the Nair infantry lock and is not in the script. The most visible smoke and muzzle flash come from OUR musket rather than as a thin volley from the Dutch wall. There is no visible heat shimmer.

fixes.correction: Make this a CLOSE shot of Ramayyan. His head and shoulders fill the left half of the wide strip. He is standing, as in the previous panel, and holds the palm-leaf bundle, with no stylus and no writing. His face is lit from below by the brass oil lamp just under the frame. Behind him to the right, smaller and softer in the background, show Varma seated on the camp stool with the whetstone lying across his knee, as in the previous panel, and ONE hand resting motionless on ONE small knife laid flat on the stone. There is only one knife: no second hilt, dagger or sheath in his other hand. Varma's face may be cut by the top edge or turned in shadow, and is never larger or more prominent than Ramayyan's. Keep the same night camp awning, distant Dutch fires and warm lamplight as the previous panel. Leave the plain awning and the dark sky above and to the right of Ramayyan's head clear for two speech balloons.
fixes.issues: This is a medium two-shot, not the scripted close shot of Ramayyan. Varma is drawn at full size beside him, not just his hand and knife behind. Ramayyan now sits writing with a stylus, but he was standing a beat earlier in 4.4. The whetstone has moved from Varma's knee to a wooden stool. Varma's right hand grips a second knife hilt while his left hand holds the knife on the stone, which muddles the panel's one prop beat (the knife gone still). Faces, costume, lamplight and the awning setting otherwise match 4.4.

fixes.correction: CORRECTION: The gun is drawn wrong: it has a second tube projecting from its breech, and the crew sponge and ram from the rear. Draw ONE smooth-bore iron muzzle-loading cannon on a wooden truck carriage. Its closed breech ends in a single round cascabel knob with nothing attached to or inserted behind it. Its muzzle is run up to an embrasure in the woven palm-mat parapet and points straight at the heart of the Dutch stockade across the sand. All loading happens at the MUZZLE end. The sponger stands beside the muzzle, his wet sheepskin sponge on a long staff just drawn out of the bore and lifted clear. The rammer man stands beside him and drives the charge home into the muzzle with a plain wooden rammer staff. The third gunner crouches behind the breech with his face visible in three-quarter view, one eye shut, squinting along the top of the barrel toward the Dutch fort against the glare, one hand on the wooden wedge (quoin) under the breech. Keep the bare-chested gunners in white mundu and white head cloths matching panel 5.1, the same palm-mat battery, the blazing sun and the clear blue sky across the top for the caption. The Dutch stockade is quiet, with no smoke rising from it. Any Dutch flag is a plain red-white-blue horizontal tricolour with no monogram.
fixes.issues: The cannon is mechanically wrong. A second tube projects from the breech of the main barrel. The sponger pushes his sponge into that rear tube, and the rammer man drives his staff into the breech end, so the gun is loaded from behind while its muzzle faces the fort. The third gunner does not squint along the barrel and has no hand on an elevation wedge: his back is to us, with his hand on the barrel at the trunnions. Smoke is also rising inside the Dutch stockade, which should be quiet before the shot.

fixes.correction: CORRECTION: Keep Nagoji on Kayal at the left exactly as drawn: same face, commander costume and still pose, looking right toward the gun. Keep the clear sky band across the top for the two captions. Fix the gun and crew. Draw ONE smooth-bore iron muzzle-loader on a wooden truck carriage. Its closed breech ends in a single round cascabel knob with no staff, rod or tube projecting from it. Its muzzle sits at an embrasure in the palm-mat parapet, pointing toward the Dutch stockade in the distance. The gun has just fired: a single large puff of white smoke and a short tongue of flame from the muzzle, with the gun and carriage visibly jolting back on their wheels. No one touches the barrel. The gunner who fired stands clear to one side, holding his linstock (a forked staff with smouldering slow match) away from the vent. The other two gunners lean back clear of the wheels, holding sponge and rammer staffs upright. The crew are the same bare-chested gunners in white mundu and white head cloths as panels 5.1 and 5.4, with no red turbans and no red sashes; the rust-red turban and red sash belong to Nagoji alone. The Dutch stockade stays quiet, with no smoke puffs or gunfire along it, so the impact stays hidden until the page turn. Any Dutch flag is a plain red-white-blue horizontal tricolour with no monogram.
fixes.issues: Nagoji on Kayal at the left is good: commander look, curled moustache, clean chin, gold ear stud, still and looking toward the gun. The gun and crew fail. A long staff projects out of the cascabel/breech of the gun as it fires (rear-loading again). A gunner has his hand on the barrel at the moment of firing, and no recoil is shown. The crew wear rust-red turbans and red sashes over sleeveless tunics, which clashes with the bare-chested gunners of 5.1 and 5.4 and borrows Nagoji's identifying colours. Several white smoke puffs along the Dutch stockade read as fire or impacts, which weakens the single shot and gives away the page-6 turn.

fixes.correction: Keep this composition and staging exactly. Kayal (bay mare, black mane, tail and lower legs, no white markings) rears in the left foreground while Nagoji hauls back on the reins, the loose end of his broad red sash whipping behind him. A blinding white-gold blast, with a pillar of flame and boiling black smoke and spinning debris, stands over the Dutch stockade and tents at upper right. Dutch soldiers are flung down in the middle distance. Our gabion trench fills the foreground with men flat and covering their heads. Fix only Nagoji's face, which is in three-quarter profile with his near ear visible under the compact rust-red turban: draw a small, flush, round gold stud clearly on that earlobe, a bright gold dot sitting on the lobe. It must not be a hanging drop or a hoop, and the lobe must not be bare. Draw his moustache as on the sheet, thick and black with the ends visibly curled, over a clean-shaven chin with no beard and no stubble.
fixes.issues: The composition is otherwise excellent: Kayal is correct (bay, black mane and legs) and rearing, Nagoji hauls on the reins with the red sash end whipping back, the glare and the smoke pillar sit over the Dutch camp, and the men in the trench are flung flat. There is no gore or text. It fails the identity check: Nagoji's near ear is clearly drawn but the lobe is bare, with no gold stud, and his moustache is thick but droops at the ends instead of curling as on the sheet. The author's 2026-10-02 decision asks for the stud to be enforced in selection.

fixes.correction: Show only the Dutch sortie and the burning wall: Dutch East India Company soldiers in blue coats and some grey coats step out through the burning gaps in the wooden palisade and dress into ranks, bayonets fixed, muskets levelled, under one plain red-white-blue horizontal tricolour with no lettering. No Travancore horsemen anywhere in the frame, no lances, no rust-red or orange turbans: all of our cavalry is hidden in the palm grove off panel and does not move until the next page. No Nair infantry running forward. If our side appears at all, it is only the top of our own earth trench parapet in the near foreground, with a few crouching Nair heads in forward-tied topknots behind round shields, facing the Dutch and not advancing. Keep the palms at the far left empty of riders, and keep the upper-left sky of drifting smoke clear and low-detail for Dhanaji's off-panel balloon. Render in the same ink-line and watercolour-wash comic style as the neighbouring panels, not photoreal painting.
fixes.issues: v01 shows the Dutch sortie through the burning palisade correctly, but it also shows the Travancore cavalry charging with levelled lances out of the palm grove, including one rider in a rust-red turban who reads as Nagoji. A foreground wave of Nair infantry is also running at the Dutch. This contradicts 7.2 (our men in the trench), 7.3 (the centre bracing to hold), 7.4 (Nagoji and all the riders still waiting in the grove) and the chapter lock that the charge lands only after the 7-to-8 page turn ('see, then ride'). The foreground Nairs have loose hair with no forward-tied topknots. The panel is rendered photoreal while 7.2 to 7.4 are ink and wash.

fixes.correction: Keep the foreground trench exactly as drawn: woven-mat revetment, posts, and Nair men ducking and falling back from the parapet behind round shields. Also keep the long bank of white musket smoke along the blue-coated Dutch firing line and the clear blue sky at upper left for the caption. Remove every horseman from the field: no cavalry, no lances, no turbaned riders of any colour, because all of our cavalry waits unseen in the palm grove and does not charge until the next page. Remove the Nair infantry running across the open ground in the middle distance. The ground between our trench and the Dutch line is empty except for dust, scrub and drifting smoke, and our men stay inside the trench. Replace the plain blue flag with a plain red-white-blue horizontal tricolour, no emblem or lettering.
fixes.issues: v01 has the right foreground (Nair men ducking behind round shields in our revetted trench), the Dutch firing line with its long bank of musket smoke, and good clear sky for the caption. In the middle distance, though, a full mounted charge with lances (one rider in an orange-red turban) and a wave of Nair infantry run across open ground at the Dutch. That pre-empts the page 8 charge and contradicts 7.3 (the centre bracing) and 7.4 (all the riders still in the grove). The Dutch flag is plain blue, not the locked plain red-white-blue tricolour.

fixes.correction: Keep Ramayyan exactly as drawn: thin, older, receding hair with curly sides, bare-headed, no shield, mud-splattered white dhoti, curved Nair sword raised, at the centre of the line. Keep the young, bare-chested Nair infantry with forward-tied topknots bracing round shields, swords and spears against the bayonets of the blue-coated Dutch on the right. Remove every mounted rider from the upper left: no horsemen, no lances, no turbans, and above all no figure in a rust-red turban or red sash, because Nagoji and all of the cavalry are hidden in the palm grove and do not charge until the next page. Fill that area with more topknotted Nair infantry, our earthwork and drifting smoke, and keep the sky at upper left and upper centre clear and low-detail for two speech balloons. Replace the two white flags over the Dutch stockade with plain red-white-blue horizontal tricolours, no lettering. No white flags anywhere, because the Dutch have not surrendered.
fixes.issues: Ramayyan matches his sheet and the ch14 row: thin, older, receding hair with curly sides, bare-headed, no shield, mud-splattered white dhoti, curved Nair sword raised at the centre of the topknotted Nair shield wall facing the blue-coat bayonets. The upper left, however, shows mounted riders galloping into battle with lances. Several wear red sashes, and one wears a rust-red turban AND a red sash in cream clothes, a Nagoji look-alike that breaks the bible rule that riders never wear that combination. It also contradicts 7.4 (Nagoji and all the riders still in the grove) and the page-8 charge. Two plain WHITE flags fly over the Dutch stockade, which reads as surrender in the middle of the sortie; Dutch flags must be red-white-blue tricolours.

fixes.correction: Keep the raised viewpoint from the palm line with the leaning palm trunk at the left edge, the burning wooden palisade at upper right, the blue-coated Dutch formation with its front ranks packed tight against the Nair shield line, and an officer's arm dragging men toward the front. Remove every horseman from the field: no Travancore cavalry anywhere, none galloping toward the thinned flank and none behind the Nair line, because Nagoji has only just seen the seam and the charge comes on the next page. The scrubland in front of the thinned flank is empty, sunlit open ground. Draw the Dutch clearly as a hollow square. The front face is packed tight against the Nair line. The rear face is packed and turned toward the burning fort. The face toward the scrubland and the viewer is reduced to a single ragged file of blue coats, with wide gaps of daylight and bare ground between the men. The Nair infantry are bare-headed with forward-tied topknots, bare chests and short white mundus, with no caps or helmets. No white flags or banners. Render in the same ink-line and watercolour-wash comic style as the neighbouring panels. Keep the upper-left sky clear and low-detail for two captions.
fixes.issues: v01 has the raised view from the palm line, the burning palisade, and the Nair line pressed against the Dutch front ranks. It even has a thinned file with an officer pulling men forward. But white-turbaned Travancore lancers are already galloping at the thinned flank on the right, and more riders charge behind the Nair line at left. That destroys the 'see, then ride' beat and the page-turn charge, and contradicts 7.4. The Dutch formation reads as a wedge or column rather than a square, with no rear face turned toward the burning fort. Some Nair infantry wear grey round caps or helmets instead of bare-headed topknots, and a plain white banner flies on our side. The rendering is painterly, not the ink-and-wash of 7.2 to 7.4.

fixes.correction: Keep everything else exactly as it is: the rider's-eye view over Kayal's bay ears and black mane, the Dutch sergeant shouting with his arm thrown out, the turning wide-eyed Dutch faces in blue coats and tricorns, the long bayonets slanting at the camera, our white-turbaned riders with spears at left and the burning wooden palisade behind. Remove the large white or pale flag on the pole at upper right. No white, grey or pale flag or banner may appear anywhere in the Dutch ranks, because it would read as surrender. If a Dutch flag is shown at all, it is a small plain horizontal red-white-blue tricolour like the one on page 7, partly hidden by smoke, with no lettering or emblem. Otherwise fill that area with smoke and fire. Keep the sky at upper left clear and low in detail for a caption.
fixes.issues: The beat works: rider's-eye view over Kayal's bay ears and black mane, the shouting sergeant with his arm out, turning Dutch faces and bayonets at angles. But a large plain white or pale-grey flag flies over the Dutch ranks at upper right. It reads as a surrender flag before the charge has even landed, and it breaks the chapter lock that Dutch flags are plain red-white-blue tricolours, as shown on page 7.

fixes.correction: Set this panel INSIDE the broken Dutch square, after the impact of 8.3, in thick dust and smoke. There is no trench, no stakes or wattle, and no Nair infantry in the foreground. Dhanaji (white Maratha pagdi, indigo quilted tunic, short black beard, no sash, talwar, brown horse) is the nearest and most central rider. He is half a length AHEAD of Nagoji, surging past Nagoji's shoulder into the gap with his sword raised high. Nagoji on Kayal (bay mare, black mane and lower legs) is just behind at Dhanaji's shoulder, in rust-red turban, cream tunic, broad red sash and boots, with thick curled moustache, CLEAN-SHAVEN chin and small gold ear stud. Deccan riders come close behind them. Scattered blue coats and dropped hats lie around the horses' legs, with no blood. In the middle distance, seen through dust, a few Dutch soldiers in blue coats and tricorns stand back to back as dark silhouettes with bayonets held out. No musket is levelled or firing. Keep the faces, costumes and horses as drawn in this version, and keep the dusty, smoky sky at the top low in detail for one caption.
fixes.issues: Nagoji and Dhanaji both match their sheets. Nagoji has the moustache, clean chin and ear stud; Dhanaji has the white pagdi, indigo tunic and beard. But the beat is wrong. The two ride side by side, still charging across open ground and our own staked trench toward an intact Dutch firing line. Muskets are levelled at Nair infantry in the right foreground. This reads as earlier than the 8.3 impact. It is not 'inside the break', Dhanaji is not half a length ahead surging past Nagoji's shoulder, and there are no Dutch soldiers silhouetted back to back. The levelled, firing muskets also contradict the caption 'Too close for their muskets.'

fixes.correction: Keep the low, ground-level full-width strip and the flintlock musket lying in trampled sand, sharp in the foreground with hoof-churned sand around it. Replace the whole background. There is no intact or ordered Dutch square, no advancing Nair infantry, no charging cavalry, and no white flags or pennants carried by anyone. Beyond the musket, in soft focus with a shallow depth of field and clearly blurred, a loose, broken scatter of Dutch soldiers in blue coats stands still with empty hands raised above their heads in surrender. A few dropped muskets and tricorn hats lie on the ground. Dust settles and thin smoke drifts from the burning wooden palisade in the far distance. The mood is still and quiet, with no motion lines and no fighting. Keep the upper band of smoky sky low in detail for one caption. No blood.
fixes.issues: The foreground works: a low, ground-level strip with a flintlock musket lying in trampled sand. The background contradicts the beat. An intact, ordered Dutch square stands with its backs to the camera, Nair infantry and cavalry are still charging in from both sides, and everything is in sharp focus rather than blurred. No hands are going up, so it is neither quiet nor 'over'. Our riders also carry white pennants, which read as surrender flags on the wrong side and are not the Travancore standard.

fixes.correction: Setting fix: the Dutch position at Colachel is a timber stockade on open sand, not a stone fort. Draw NO masonry wall, no stone rampart, and no rocky bluff or cliff behind the beach. The background is a low sandy bank topped by what is left of the palisade of upright sharpened logs, burned down to blackened, broken stumps and fallen charred timbers glowing with embers. Show only small, low flames and rising smoke, matching the burned palisade on the sand slope in the following panels, with no figures standing on the ruins. Give every Dutch survivor dark or grey-brown hair, with no tall, pale-haired man among them, because De Lannoy first appears in the next panel. Keep everything else that worked: the wide framing; the lurid purple and red sunset with the sun on the sea horizon at left and distant sailing ships; the Dutch survivors in ash-stained blue coats huddled on the beach, some kneeling with heads bowed and some standing hollow-eyed with hands raised; the Travancore guards in white mundu with spears at the edges; and the large, clear sky at upper left for the caption.
fixes.issues: v01 shows the right beat (purple and red sunset through smoke, ash-stained blue-coat survivors kneeling and standing with hands raised, Nair guards, and clear sky at upper left for the caption), but the setting is wrong. The Dutch position is drawn as a tall stone masonry rampart on a rocky bluff with Travancore men standing on top. On pages 6 to 8 and in panels 9.2 to 9.5, the same position is a wooden palisade on a sandy bank. The stockade is also still standing and burning with tall flames, not burned down to embers as the script says. A pale-haired, bare-headed man standing in the centre with his hands raised could also be read as De Lannoy before his walk-out in 9.2.

fixes.correction: Frame this as a tight close-up, head and shoulders only, of Marthanda Varma still seated on his horse exactly as in the panel before (only the top of the horse's neck and the gold-studded bridle at the lower frame edge). Use the varma-v1 face: jet-black hair with no grey, thick curled moustache, the red Vaishnavite forehead mark and pearl drop earrings. He wears the same campaign court look as panels 10.2 and 10.4: a cream-and-gold wrapped turban with the jewelled peacock-feather crest, bare chest, cream-and-gold cloth over the left shoulder and layered gold bead necklaces. Never show him bare-headed, with loose or side-knotted hair, or standing on foot. His expression is still and unhurried, eyes level, looking off-panel toward the prisoners. Light the near side of his face with a warm red-orange glow from the burning fort's embers and leave the other side in cool blue twilight shadow. Behind him keep only soft dusk sky and blurred smoke, with no other figures near his head. Leave clear, low-detail sky above and beside his head for two speech balloons. No text or letters anywhere in the image.
fixes.issues: v01 fails the script beat and page continuity. 10.3 calls for 'Varma, close', but this is a three-quarter-length figure in a wide beach shot full of guards and prisoners. Varma stands on foot, while 10.2 and 10.4 show him mounted and 10.4 has him turning his horse away. He is bare-headed with loose hair and grey streaks, while 10.2 and 10.4 show the cream-and-gold turban with the peacock crest. The grey is also off-sheet for 1741, since varma-v1 has black hair. The 'embers red on one side of his face' lighting is replaced by general sunset light.
